prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the exact same line in src/mcp/server/stdio.py — the `write_stream` memory-object-stream creation, currently hardcoded to buffer_size=0. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2654 fixes the bug directly by changing the write_stream buffer default from 0 to 1, so the fix applies out-of-the-box with no caller changes required; it also adds a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact blocking scenario (final response queued while a progress notification is still being flushed). #2215 instead adds two new keyword parameters (read_stream_buffer_size, write_stream_buffer_size) but leaves the default at 0, so the underlying blocking behavior is unchanged unless a caller opts in by explicitly passing write_stream_buffer_size=1 — it does not fix the reported problem by default. #2215's diff is also broader (touches both read and write stream construction plus the public function signature) versus #2654's single-line default change with an explanatory comment. Merging both would conflict on the same create_memory_object_stream call; #2654's targeted default fix supersedes the need for #2215's opt-in knob for this specific bug.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: `OAuthContext.lock` is held across the entire `async_auth_flow` handling, including while a request is yielded back to httpx — for long-running requests (e.g. an SSE GET long-poll) this blocks all other concurrent requests through the same provider from acquiring the lock for unrelated state checks/refreshes. (2 PRs)
members.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: `OAuthContext.lock` is held across the entire `async_auth_flow` handling, including while a request is yielded back to httpx — for long-running requests (e.g. an SSE GET long-poll) this blocks all other concurrent requests through the same provider from acquiring the lock for unrelated state checks/refreshes. (2 PRs)
members.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs split the single `lock` into a short-lived state lock plus a second single-flight lock for refresh/reauth transitions (`refresh_lock` in #2858, `flow_lock` in #3243), narrowing what's held while a request is yielded. #3243 additionally changes the lock primitive itself from `anyio.Lock` to `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)`, with an added comment explaining that httpx can resume or close an auth-flow async generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock, and `anyio.Lock` enforces same-task release (raising on the trio backend if violated). #2858 keeps both `lock` and the new `refresh_lock` as `anyio.Lock`, so it narrows the critical section but doesn't address that task-ownership mismatch scenario that #3243's semaphore-based change specifically targets.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(request_id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id "1" into the same key — this can produce a false-positive 409 (rejecting a legitimate concurrent request whose id only collides after stringification) or still cross-wire responses in that collision case. #3221 fixes this by adding `_request_stream_key()`, a type-preserving key (`i:` prefix for int, `s:` prefix for str, with an explicit bool exclusion since bool subclasses int) so numeric and string ids with the same textual form no longer collide, and also explicitly guards against a string id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 is a strict superset fix for the same bug #3063 targets.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id cross-wire into the same `_request_streams` slot: the second request silently overwrites the first one's routing entry, so one request receives the other's response payload and the other hangs. Both PRs add a check that rejects a request id that is already in flight before allocating its stream.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(request_id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id "1" into the same key — this can produce a false-positive 409 (rejecting a legitimate concurrent request whose id only collides after stringification) or still cross-wire responses in that collision case. #3221 fixes this by adding `_request_stream_key()`, a type-preserving key (`i:` prefix for int, `s:` prefix for str, with an explicit bool exclusion since bool subclasses int) so numeric and string ids with the same textual form no longer collide, and also explicitly guards against a string id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 is a strict superset fix for the same bug #3063 targets.
